# Menu

Action menu on the native Popover API top layer: the top layer and light dismiss come from the platform; Esc, roving keyboard, placement and dismissal reasons are Psi's (D53). Controlled-only, like Dialog (D50). Controlled-only means Menu does not change its own visibility. Esc and item-select *report* a dismissal via onClose(reason) and leave the popover open; only the consumer flipping `open` to false actually closes it. Esc calls preventDefault() to suppress the platform's own popover dismissal, which is what makes that possible. Light dismiss (outside click) is the one asymmetry, and it is forced by the platform: the browser hides the popover itself and the hide-side `beforetoggle` is not cancelable, so the popover is already closed by the time the resulting `toggle` lets us report onClose("outside"). The consumer must still flip `open` to false so React's state matches the DOM. `toggle` therefore reports only that one reason. A close driven by the consumer (`open` true -> false) runs through the sync effect's own hidePopover(), which raises a `toggle` too — that one is suppressed, because a programmatic close is not a dismissal and must not call onClose.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | — | yes | Controlled open state; syncs to showPopover()/hidePopover(). |
| `onClose` | `(reason: MenuCloseReason) => void` | — | yes | Called when a dismissal is *requested*; the consumer flips `open`. Menu never closes itself on `"esc"` or `"item-select"` — the popover stays open until `open` becomes false (D50). `"outside"` is the one exception: light dismiss is performed by the browser before it tells us, so by the time that reason is reported the popover is already closed. Flipping `open` to false is still required, to keep React's state in step. Invariant (D58): a dismissal is only ever reported for a menu that is currently open according to its own `open` prop. The platform can close an auto popover before the consumer's state catches up — clicking another menu's trigger light-dismisses this one before the consumer's click handler runs — and a report for an already-closed menu would clear a selection that has since moved on. `"tab"` (D102): Tab or Shift Tab inside the open menu. Focus moves on to the next control as the browser moves it; the consumer flips `open`. |
| `onFocusReturn` | `((event: FocusReturnEvent<"close">) => void)` | — | no | Called when the menu closes while focus is inside it and Psi is about to return focus to the trigger (D147): `event.target` is the trigger. Focus your own element in the handler to take over, or call `preventDefault()` to leave focus where it is. Not called after a light dismiss or Tab moved focus elsewhere. See the Focus guide. |
| `trigger` | `ReactElement<Record<string, unknown>, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | — | yes | The trigger element. Must be a single React element that spreads unknown props onto a focusable node (a Psi `Button`, say): Menu clones it to add `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, so assistive tech associates the menu with the control users actually focus. |
| `placement` | `"bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "top-start" \| "top-end"` | bottom-start | no | Placement relative to the trigger. |
| `id` | `string` | — | no | The menu element's id, which the trigger's `aria-controls` names (D102). Generated when absent. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | no | Accessible name for the menu when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | no | The id of a `MenuText` (or any element) that describes the menu (D99). Unset by default: a description may be spoken every time the menu opens. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | yes | MenuItem, MenuSeparator and MenuText children. |
| `className` | `string` | — | no | Additional CSS class name(s) merged onto the component's root element. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | — | no | Forwarded ref to the popover element. |

## Keyboard & assistive tech

| Keys | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Arrow Down / Arrow Up | Moves between items, wrapping at both ends. Disabled items are reachable, so a user learns they exist, and cannot be activated (D131). |
| Home / End | Jumps to the first or last item. |
| Any single printable key | Typeahead — focuses the first item whose label starts with the typed prefix; the prefix resets after 500ms. Keystrokes with Meta/Ctrl/Alt held are ignored. |
| Esc | Suppresses the platform's own dismissal and reports onClose("esc"); the menu stays open until the consumer flips `open` (D50). |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused item (native button behavior). |
| Arrow Down / Arrow Up on the closed trigger | Opens the menu on its first / last item by clicking the trigger, since Menu cannot open itself; the consumer's onClick flips `open` (D102). |
| Tab / Shift Tab | Reports onClose("tab") and lets focus move on to the next control; the consumer flips `open`, and focus is not pulled back to the trigger (D102). |

Opens on the native top layer via popover="auto", which supplies light dismiss. Controlled-only: every dismissal path (esc, item-select, outside) only reports onClose(reason) — the consumer must flip `open` to actually close it; outside is the one path the platform has already acted on by the time it is reported. Opening moves focus to the first item — Menu takes focus off the trigger as soon as `open` becomes true. A re-render that removes the focused item moves focus to the item now at its position, or the last item; an emptied menu holds focus itself (tabindex=-1, never a Tab stop), so Esc and Tab still report their own reasons (D131). Focus returns to the trigger when the menu actually closes, and only if focus is still inside the menu, so a light dismiss onto another control does not steal focus back. Requires an accessible name — pass aria-label. Placement uses CSS anchor positioning where supported and a JS fallback below that floor; below it there is no collision flip. Past --psi-menu-max-height (the shared --psi-popup-max-height, 320px) the menu scrolls and the focused item stays in view; a menu taller than the room on both sides of its trigger opens on the larger side and fills it (D131). onFocusReturn reports the return of focus to the trigger, reason "close", and can take it over or decline it (D147).

## Theming

Override `--psi-menu-*` custom properties at any scope; interactive states derive automatically (L - 0.04 hover, L - 0.08 active).



## Rules

- One accent per visual group; everything else neutral or ghost.
- danger only for actions with real consequences.
- Sizes are px numbers (24|32|40|48), never S/M/L.
- Typography tokens are --psi-text-{size}-{lineHeight}-{weight}.
- Override component tokens (--psi-{component}-*), not semantic tokens, for one-off theming.
- --psi-button-font overrides button typography across all sizes (documented D34 override; ember → mono).
- Wrap labeled form controls in Field — label association, description/error line, aria-describedby and aria-invalid come wired; don't hand-roll label+message rows.
- Field is for a control with a *visible* label. A toolbar filter control named by aria-label or placeholder takes neither a Field nor a hand-rolled label row — compare filter-toolbar (no labels) with table-pagination ("Rows per page" visible, so Field). Filters with visible labels submitted together by a Find button are filter-form: a Toolbar as="form" align="start" of Fields with one-line labels, where a field's error line is the Field's own and hangs below its control (D87, D92).
- Label beside its control: <Field labelPosition="start"> for one field in a toolbar or pager (keep Toolbar align="center"); <FieldStack labelPosition="start"> for a form whose labels share one column, as wide as the longest label up to --psi-field-label-max-width, stacking below 480px of the form's width. A theme sets --psi-field-label-align: end to put labels against their controls (D115).
- Width of a control: <Field controlWidth={80|120|160|240|320|480}> sizes the control it wraps in px and lets it shrink in a narrower column; the label and message keep the Field's width. Pick the step from the value: at size 32 an Input fits about 7/12/17/26/36/55 digits (an ICCID's 20 digits → 240; a page-size Select → 80). Without it the control fills the Field. A FieldStack stops at --psi-field-stack-max-width (640px). In a Toolbar, the control of a top-labelled Field without controlWidth takes --psi-toolbar-control-width (200px), as a bare control does, so filter-form and date-range-filter rows are even; controlWidth replaces it, and a side-labelled Field (Rows per page) keeps its content width (D135).
- A popup's maximum height is --psi-popup-max-height (320px), shared by every popup through its own alias (--psi-menu-max-height, --psi-combobox-popup-max-height); past it the popup scrolls. Override the alias for one component, the shared token for all (D131).
- Select for a short fixed list; Combobox when the list is long enough to search, or more than one value is picked (D130). Combobox takes options as data ({value, label, description?, disabled?}), filters as the user types, and with multiple shows the picked values as Tags. Select has no multiple.
- Use Dialog for blocking modal flows — title/footer slots, dismissible gate; danger stays on the footer Buttons, one accent per group.
- Text links are Link (React) or the .psi-link class on any <a>: accent colour, underlined at rest, never by colour alone (D119). A router app passes its own link as Link's only child. Button href is for an action that should look like a button. Inside a NavItem or among NavBar's links, pass your router link itself, not Link.
- Pick between Tabs, SegmentedControl and RadioGroup by the job (D132). Switch 2–4 views of one region compactly (Map/Trace, Preview/Code): <Tabs> with a <SegmentedControl aria-label> (no value: Tabs owns it) of <Segment>s in place of TabList, outside the TabPanels, plus a TabPanel per segment. Switch page sections, more than 4 views, or a vertical list: Tabs + TabList + Tab. Pick one of 2–4 short options that applies at once (Light/Dark/System, a theme): <SegmentedControl aria-label value onValueChange>, a radio group wherever it sits (value makes it one). A value a form submits, options with descriptions, or more than 4: RadioGroup (Select for many). An action: Button or Toolbar. Segment labels are one or two words; the control never wraps, and truncates them when its container is narrower; fill shares the width equally. Sizes 24|32|40.
- A count after a label is Count (D124): neutral by default; tone="attention" is a pill and should carry a label ("4 stuck"), since the tone is visual. A Count is never a live region. In a NavTree, pass it as NavItem's count, and an icon as icon on NavItem or NavGroup; the icon is decorative and sized by the tree.
